name: Table
propertyCopy: Corner radius, size and the header row are properties of the same component, not separate tables - change them below to check this table's types and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Table displays structured data across fixed columns, like an admin data grid or a report view - rows and columns that let a user compare values across many records at once, unlike List's simpler stacked-row layout with no column alignment. When to Use An admin data grid or user management list - structured records compared across shared columns. Order history or a report/analytics view - tabular data where column alignment aids comparison. An inventory listing - any dataset naturally organized into consistent fields per row. When Not to Use A simple stack of similar items with no meaningful column structure - use List instead - Table's column overhead isn't worth it for unstructured rows. A small number of visually distinct content blocks - use Card or a grid of Cards. Data better suited to a single set of label/value pairs - use Description for one record's details rather than a one-row table. Best Practices Keep column headers concise and consistently aligned with their column's data type (numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned). Support sorting on columns where order genuinely helps comparison, and clearly indicate the active sort. Pair large tables with pagination, virtualized scrolling, or both - virtualize once a table is showing 500+ rows, rather than rendering thousands of rows at once. Do and Don't Do NameStatusAria ChenActiveLeo FischerInvited Column headers that name exactly one kind of value each, so every cell in a column is comparable to the one above it. Don't DetailsAria Chen - active - joined Jan 2024 - adminLeo Fischer, invited, pending since last week Collapsing several fields into one free-text column removes the ability to sort, filter or scan by any single attribute - it stops being a table. Accessibility Uses real table semantics (thead/tbody/th with proper scope), so screen readers can announce row/column context for each cell. Sortable column headers are real, keyboard-operable buttons that announce the current sort direction. Row selection checkboxes are independently labeled with which row they apply to. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header sets aria-sort="ascending", aria-sort="descending" or aria-sort="none" and announces the change - a visual arrow icon alone is not sufficient.
